citations.quote:
Put $K=\mathbb Q(q)$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $p=q+q^{-1}$ and $h=q^2+q^{-2}$. For $k\ge0$ set

$$n_{2k}=8k+2,\qquad n_{2k+1}=8k+4,\qquad \ell_{2k}=2,\qquad\ell_{2k+1}=4,\qquad r_j=\ell_j-1,$$

and set $p_j=p$ for even $j$ and $p_j=h$ for odd $j$. Let $u_{j,a}=F^{(a)}u_{j,0}$, $0\le a\le n_j$, be the divided basis of the highest string $V(n_j)$, of weight $n_j-2a$. On the algebraic module $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}V(n_j)$ define

$$T_j u_{j,t\ell_j}=(-1)^t u_{j+1,r_j+t\ell_j}\quad(0\le t\le n_j/\ell_j),$$

and define $T_j$ to be zero on all other divided basis vectors. Put $S=\sum_jT_j/p_j$, $C=1+S$, and $b_{j,a}=C u_{j,a}$.

Then $S^2=0$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$; these are finite-column algebraic operators. The homogeneous basis $B=\{b_{j,a}\}$ has a free $U_A$-stable integral span, its standard compatible bar fixes $B$, and its regular zero and infinity charts and crystal residues are those of the standard direct sum of divided strings. Thus it is an actual four-axiom based integrable finite-Cartan-type module, with a balanced integral triple and no choice assumption.

For every $J\ge0$, the finite version $M^{(J)}=\bigoplus_{0\le j\le J}V(n_j)$, with shears only for $j<J$, has the same properties. For every $a\in U_A$ the raw-coordinate action is $C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS$; its column at a raw basis vector of index $j$ is supported at summand indices at most $j+2$. That column agrees with the finite version whenever $J\ge j+2$.

The raw seed $b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$ in two copies has total weight zero and factor weights $2,-2$. Both factors are deformed: $b_{0,0}=u_{0,0}+u_{1,1}/p$ and $b_{0,2}=u_{0,2}-u_{1,3}/p$. This statement constructs the modules and finite versions; it does not assert infinite tensor correction supports.

Use the actual periodic modules, basis $b_{j,a}$, finite cuts $M^{(J)}$, denominators $p=q+q^{-1}$ and $h=q^2+q^{-2}=p^2-2$ of [[lem-two-cyclotomic-shears-give-a-periodic-integrable-based-sl-two-chain]]. On $M^{(J)}\otimes M^{(J)}$ use the rank-one tensor bar $\Psi=\Theta(\bar{\phantom{x}}\otimes\bar{\phantom{x}})$, with

$$\Theta=\sum_{r\ge0}a_r E^{(r)}\otimes F^{(r)},\qquad a_r=q^{-r}\prod_{s=1}^r(q^{2s}-1).$$

There is a unique normalized bar-fixed lift $G^{(J)}$ of the raw seed $b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$: its seed coefficient is $1$ and every other coefficient belongs to $q\mathbb Z[q]$, with corrections strictly increasing the first factor weight. Let $f_j^{(J)}$ be its coefficient at $b_{j,0}\otimes b_{j,n_j}$, for $j\le J$. These coefficients agree as the cut increases. In the Laurent polynomial quotient over $\mathbb Q$ they satisfy

$$f_{2k+1}^{(J)}\equiv(-1)^k(2k+1)!(q^3-q)\pmod{q^4+1},\qquad f_{2k}^{(J)}\equiv(-1)^k2(2k+1)!\pmod{q^2+1}\quad(k\ge1).$$

In particular $f_J^{(J)}\ne0$ for every $J\ge1$. Thus the normalized corrections escape every finite constituent cut; this is a claim about the corrected lifts, not merely about repeated raw-bar closure. All constructions and proofs are choice free.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

derivations.claim: **Actual based factors and the raw seed.** Take two copies of the module in [F1]. These are actual finite-Cartan-type integrable modules satisfying all four based axioms, with the specified stable free integral lattices and crystal charts. The raw seed is $e=b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$, of factor weights $2,-2$ and total weight zero. In standard coordinates its two factors are $u_{0,0}+u_{1,1}/(q+q^{-1})$ and $u_{0,2}-u_{1,3}/(q+q^{-1})$, so both factors carry genuine deformations. The constituent lengths grow without bound, and the module is outside the globally bounded highest/lowest classes. Every vector still lies in finitely many finite standard constituents.

**The full tensor bar is finite, integral and triangular.** On each input vector, only finitely many standard constituent pairs occur. Their finite strings bound all nonzero divided $E^{(r)}$ and $F^{(r)}$ actions, so [F3] evaluates as a finite sum. Each scalar $a_r$ is Laurent integral and each divided action preserves the actual integral factor lattices by [F1]; hence $\Psi$ preserves their algebraic tensor lattice. Unitarity and the standard compatible factor bars make $\Psi^2=1$. Its raw matrix is $(C^{-1}\otimes C^{-1})\Theta(C\otimes C)$ followed by coefficient bar. The degree-zero term is exactly the identity, and every other term strictly raises the first weight because the shears preserve weights. All columns are finite. Thus this example retains the full integral-action and field-bar assertions.

**Exact projection to a finite cut.** In raw coordinates let $\pi_J$ kill tuples with a factor index exceeding $J$ and identify the remaining raw indices with those of $M^{(J)}\otimes M^{(J)}$. Each shear raises a constituent index; standard divided actions preserve constituent indices. Therefore every path in the raw bar expansion raises indices or preserves them, and deleting indices above $J$ gives exactly the bar expansion with the last outgoing shear omitted. Equivalently standard constituent projection commutes with $\Theta$, and its compositions with $C$ and $C^{-1}$ are their finite-cut versions. Consequently $\pi_J\Psi=\Psi^{(J)}\pi_J$. This is an identity of the complete finite-column raw matrices; it does not assume that intersecting a cyclic field submodule gives a balanced restriction.

**No finite normalized fixed lift.** Suppose $g$ were a finite-support fixed vector with $g-e$ having coefficients in $q\mathbb Z[q]$. Let $K$ be the largest factor index in its support and take $J\ge K+2$. Its projection is the same finite coefficient vector, is fixed by step 2.1 and has the required seed residue. It equals $G^{(J)}$: indeed the difference is a finite fixed vector whose every coefficient is in $q\mathbb Z[q]$; at its least first weight, triangularity forces each coefficient to equal its own bar, impossible for a nonzero strictly positive polynomial. Thus the difference vanishes. But the projected candidate has zero coefficient at $b_{J,0}\otimes b_{J,n_J}$, whereas [F2] proves that coefficient nonzero in $G^{(J)}$. This contradiction disproves existence of $g$, even without imposing a strict-transfer condition on its proposed corrections.

**Failure of the integral balanced map.** Put $\mathcal M=M_A\otimes_A M_A$, $L=L_0\otimes_{A_0}L_0$ and $L^-=\Psi(L)$, the actual infinity chart. Their raw coefficient rings give $\mathcal M\cap L=\bigoplus\mathbb Z[q](b\otimes b')$. There is no nonzero $\Psi$-anti-invariant vector in this intersection: at its least first weight an anti-invariant finite vector would have a polynomial coefficient $c$ with $\bar c=-c$, forcing $c=0$, a contradiction. Every vector $v$ in $\mathcal M\cap L\cap L^-$ is therefore fixed: both $v$ and $\Psi v$ belong to $\mathcal M\cap L$, and $\Psi v-v$ is anti-invariant. If reduction from that triple intersection to $(\mathcal M\cap L)/(\mathcal M\cap qL)$ were onto the raw residue class of $e$, its preimage would be such a fixed finite vector congruent to $e$ with positive-polynomial corrections, contradicting step 3.1. Hence the actual integral tensor reduction map fails surjectivity.

**Conclusion and boundary.** Two genuine four-axiom based integrable $A_1$ modules thus have a finite-column integral involutive triangular quasi-$R$ tensor bar but no algebraic normalized global correction for the specified raw seed. In particular no tensor global basis with the promised finite transitions can exist, and the integral tensor triple fails the balanced reduction property explicitly exhibited in step 4.1. Finite-dimensional products, bounded highest/lowest constructions and separately compatible finite-cut direct limits are not refuted; the counterexample concerns the unqualified arbitrary based finite-type tensor assertion. Every index, module and map is explicit and all arguments use finite arithmetic or induction, with no choice assumption.

boundaries.reason: The universal assertion is refuted by an explicit nonempty pair and seed.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.2 treats the degree-zero identity and all zero divided string endpoint actions; step 4.1 proves the absence of nonzero anti-invariant integral chart vectors.
Step 1.1 specifies the one raw seed with nonzero field factors, and step 3.1 refutes a normalized lift of this singleton.
Step 1.1 uses genuine free based lattices and nonzero denominators; F2 and step 3.1 use nonzero characteristic-zero residues at every positive cut.
Step 3.1 compares with the explicitly nonzero last-constituent top/bottom coordinate; F1 checks every finite divided-power string endpoint.
Step 3.1 takes the explicit integer J=K+2 after the finite maximum K; step 5.1 records that every vector and index is specified without any choice principle.

risk_review.notes: Local complete counterexample authoring, not native independent acceptance. Fully read and independently verified the actual four-axiom periodic module and the complete all-cut 11-step factorial/pole recurrence. Exact raw-cut projection transfers any finite candidate to every larger cut; positive-polynomial uniqueness contradicts the forced last coordinate. The separate anti-invariant argument proves failure of balanced-map surjectivity. Integral ACTION and field tensor-bar properties remain valid; no abstract triangular matrix or mere raw-support graph substitutes for the actual counterexample.
